correctness.rationale: The exact affine recurrence yields the positive-branch trigonometric formula. At the chosen trigonometric centers, the positive-branch iterate equals one and has an explicitly calculated strictly positive derivative. A shrinking interval permits uniform derivative control and two unique roots, with all earlier branch iterates positive. The mean-value theorem produces a sharp exponentially small gap with controlled relative error; subtracting adjacent center parameters gives the inverse-cubic neighboring threshold separation. High-precision computations check small instances but are not used to prove the theorem.

value.rationale: The period-adding/reset-window phenomenon is explicitly motivated in the originating dynamical-systems literature. It is not evident from numerical endpoint tables that complementary parameter gaps are exponentially, rather than polynomially, thin. The theorem gives a parameter-independent leading constant, demonstrates a fundamental exponential/polynomial scale separation as the parameter approaches four from below, and controls all sufficiently large branch-exit thresholds; it is a motivated quantitative bifurcation law.
